title: A-B-A frames resume the same active referent
summary: Test whether exact A-B-A windows encode an interruption: the second A resumes the same active item or target after B, rather than being a generic repeated whole. The question is referent continuity, not a translation of A or B.

design.mechanism: B is a bounded intervening operation or qualification; repeated A reactivates the prior referent and inherits its slot.
design.unit: cached exact A-B-A window with owner/target and structural-slot annotations
design.contrast: A-B-A versus matched A-B-C and A-C-A windows with the same lengths and section
design.prediction: The two A positions preserve owner/target and compatible slot tags more often than both controls, across held folios.
design.scope: cached complete fields and admitted owner-spine records; feasibility unknown until independent referent bindings exist on at least five physical folios
design.countermodel: A-B-A is a layout or template recurrence with no referential continuity; A positions should then match controls after section/position adjustment.
design.binding: independent source or visual owner links for both A positions, with ambiguous crossings quarantined
design.related: SIDEQUEST_semantic_aba_return_frame; GDT573 anaphoric phrase route; retained as a distinct window-level referent test
